The 2024 disclosures cover the landscape of AI model investment (LLMs, SLMs, etc.), their disruption of user experiences, and the strategic view that these models must run on-device for privacy and utility. The 2025 disclosure (qcom_2025_1_D010) covers the exact same specific points: the development of LLMs/SLMs/LVMs/LMMs, their disruption of search/content, and the necessity of on-device execution for utility, privacy, and security. qcom_2024_1_D011 maps to the model landscape/disruption, and qcom_2024_1_D012 maps to the on-device necessity/utility argument found in qcom_2025_1_D010.

The 2024 disclosure expects continued advancement in edge device generative AI capabilities and increased adoption. The 2025 disclosure (qcom_2025_1_D010) contains the specific sentence: 'We expect continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices and increased adoption of generative AI capable technologies in handsets and other edge devices.' This is a direct textual and topical match.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD completed the acquisition of Silo AI in 2024, expanding its AI model development capabilities and gaining a software stack for training large language models on AMD Instinct accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the acceleration and development of AI models, specifically Large Language Models (LLMs). Qualcomm notes 'significant investment... in the development of complex large language models (LLMs)... which are beginning to change the landscape of the user experience.' AMD discusses its acquisition of Silo AI to 'accelerate development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware' and notes that Silo AI developed a software stack to 'train multiple state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) on AMD Instinct accelerators.' Both are deeply involved in the AI model development lifecycle, with Qualcomm focusing on the market trend and model types, and AMD focusing on the hardware/software infrastructure enabling that training.

sentences.text: Significant investment continues across many industries in the development of complex large language models (LLMs), more tailored small language models (SLMs), large vision models (LVMs), large multimodal models (LMMs) and other generative AI models, which are beginning to change the landscape of the user experience.

LLMs and SLMs (e.g., GPT-4o and Llama3) are used for text-based natural language processing applications such as answering queries, document summarization and creation, LVMs (e.g., Stable Diffusion and ControlNet) are used for image and video processing, and LMMs are used to understand and process multiple types of data inputs or modalities such as text and images.
The acquisition of Silo AI expanded our capability to accelerate development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware.

Silo AI has also developed a software stack used to train multiple state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) on AMD Instinct accelerators that can accelerate the development of highly-performant AMD training solutions.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Tanzu Platform accelerates software delivery with enhanced governance and operational efficiency, includes Tanzu AI Solutions for generative AI applications, and offers full-stack visibility and lifecycle management across clouds.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the delivery of AI-powered applications and intelligent features. Qualcomm highlights that generative AI models are 'beginning to change the landscape of the user experience' and offering 'enhancements in consumer utility.' Broadcom describes its Tanzu AI Solutions as helping 'application teams deliver generative AI-powered, intelligent applications quickly, safely, and at scale.' Both recognize the market demand for integrated AI capabilities in applications, with Qualcomm focusing on the end-user impact and Broadcom on the software/platform infrastructure to deliver these apps.

sentences.text: Significant investment continues across many industries in the development of complex large language models (LLMs), more tailored small language models (SLMs), large vision models (LVMs), large multimodal models (LMMs) and other generative AI models, which are beginning to change the landscape of the user experience.

• Tanzu Platform: This cloud native application platform accelerates software delivery, providing platform engineering teams with enhanced governance and operational efficiency while reducing toil and complexity for development teams. Tanzu Platform includes access to content including enterprise-ready curated distributions of open source software technologies used for storing and processing data. It also includes Tanzu AI Solutions, a set of capabilities that help application teams deliver generative AI-powered, intelligent applications quickly, safely, and at scale. Tanzu Platform also offers teams full-stack visibility from applications to infrastructure and efficient modern application lifecycle management across public and private clouds with Cloud Foundry and/or with any conformant Kubernetes.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel views AI as a generational shift and aims to bring AI to where data is generated and used, addressing the full AI continuum from GenAI to AI PCs and edge computing. The company leverages a spectrum of hardware and software platforms for open, modular solutions and is infusing AI into its technologies to support current and future workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies frame AI as a fundamental shift in computing infrastructure, though Qualcomm focuses on the specific model types and user experience disruption while Intel focuses on the strategic continuum from cloud to edge. Qualcomm notes that LLMs, SLMs, LVMs, and LMMs are 'beginning to change the landscape of the user experience' and 'disrupting traditional methods of search, content creation, recommendation systems and personalized digital assistants.' Similarly, Intel states that 'AI represents a generational shift in computing by expanding human abilities' and aims to 'address every phase of the AI continuum, from the largest, most challenging GenAI and large language models to emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge.' Both identify Large Language Models (LLMs) and recommendation/content systems as key drivers, but Qualcomm emphasizes the on-device/user experience angle while Intel emphasizes the full-stack infrastructure strategy.

sentences.text: Significant investment continues across many industries in the development of complex large language models (LLMs), more tailored small language models (SLMs), large vision models (LVMs), large multimodal models (LMMs) and other generative AI models, which are beginning to change the landscape of the user experience.

They are disrupting traditional methods of search, content creation, recommendation systems and personalized digital assistants, offering significant enhancements in consumer utility and productivity.
We also seek to address every phase of the AI continuum, from the largest, most challenging GenAI and large language models to emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge.
We believe AI represents a generational shift in computing by expanding human abilities and solving the most challenging problems.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, Intel launched the Intel Gaudi 3 AI accelerators, offering significant price-performance advantages for AI inference applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss AI accelerators and hardware enabling AI workloads, but Qualcomm describes the broad ecosystem of model types (LLMs, SLMs, etc.) changing user experiences, whereas Intel highlights a specific product launch (Gaudi 3) for inference. Qualcomm states that 'Significant investment continues... in the development of complex large language models (LLMs)... which are beginning to change the landscape of the user experience.' Intel notes that 'In 2024, we launched the Intel® Gaudi® 3 AI accelerators offering significant price-performance advantages for AI inference applications.' While both address the AI compute landscape, Qualcomm's disclosure is about the transformative impact of model diversity on end-user applications, while Intel's is about specific hardware execution for inference tasks.

sentences.text: Significant investment continues across many industries in the development of complex large language models (LLMs), more tailored small language models (SLMs), large vision models (LVMs), large multimodal models (LMMs) and other generative AI models, which are beginning to change the landscape of the user experience.
▪Datacenter AI accelerators and GPUs. In 2024, we launched the Intel® Gaudi® 3 AI accelerators offering significant price-performance advantages for AI inference applications.

comparisons.peer_summary: The graphics market is driven by AI, VR/AR, and high-resolution gaming needs; the company announced GDDR7 in 2024, completing its industry-leading portfolio for AI inference on CPUs, NPUs, and GPUs.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify AI as a primary driver for graphics and high-performance memory markets. Qualcomm discusses how generative AI models are 'disrupting traditional methods of... recommendation systems' and changing user experience, which often relies on high-bandwidth data processing. Micron explicitly links its graphics memory products to AI, stating that 'Our GDDR6 and GDDR6X DRAM graphics products are incorporated into... graphics processing unit-based data center solutions, which are the driving force behind applications such as AI...'. Additionally, Micron notes that 'The addition of GDDR7 completes our industry-leading product portfolio for AI inference applications,' directly addressing the inference needs enabled by the AI models Qualcomm describes.

sentences.text: They are disrupting traditional methods of search, content creation, recommendation systems and personalized digital assistants, offering significant enhancements in consumer utility and productivity.

Our GDDR6 and GDDR6X DRAM graphics products are incorporated into gaming consoles, PC graphics cards, and graphics processing unit-based data center solutions, which are the driving force behind applications such as AI, virtual and augmented reality, 4K and 8K gaming, and professional design.
The addition of GDDR7 completes our industry-leading product portfolio for AI inference applications on CPUs, neural processing units, and graphics processing units.

comparisons.peer_topic: PC Market AI Capabilities and Client SSD Portfolio Expansion
comparisons.peer_summary: Next-generation PCs require higher performance SSDs due to AI capabilities; SBU expanded its portfolio in 2024 with the 3500 NVMe SSD built on Micron G8 NAND, targeting demanding business and consumer workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the impact of AI on PC client devices. Qualcomm notes that generative AI is 'disrupting traditional methods of search, content creation... and personalized digital assistants,' enhancing consumer utility. Micron states that 'The next generation PCs contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI capabilities and require higher performance and higher average capacity SSDs.' Both recognize that AI features in client devices are driving new hardware requirements, with Qualcomm focusing on the software/application experience and Micron on the storage infrastructure needed to support it.

sentences.text: They are disrupting traditional methods of search, content creation, recommendation systems and personalized digital assistants, offering significant enhancements in consumer utility and productivity.
PC: The next generation PCs contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI capabilities and require higher performance and higher average capacity SSDs than traditional PCs.

comparisons.peer_summary: GPU parallel processing capabilities are essential for deep learning, enabling AI solutions like generative AI and recommendation systems to deliver services difficult or impossible with traditional coding.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies explicitly discuss the role of AI, specifically generative AI and recommendation systems, in transforming computing and user experiences. Qualcomm states that generative AI models are 'disrupting traditional methods of search, content creation, recommendation systems and personalized digital assistants.' NVIDIA echoes this, listing 'generative AI, which can create new content such as text, code, images, audio, video... and recommendation systems, which can recommend highly relevant content... using deep neural networks' as examples of GPU-powered AI solutions. Both identify these specific applications as central to the current AI landscape.

sentences.text: They are disrupting traditional methods of search, content creation, recommendation systems and personalized digital assistants, offering significant enhancements in consumer utility and productivity.

Examples include generative AI, which can create new content such as text, code, images, audio, video, and molecule structures, and recommendation systems, which can recommend highly relevant content such as products, services, media or ads using deep neural networks trained on vast datasets that capture the user preferences.

comparisons.peer_summary: The NVIDIA RTX platform enables real-time rendering of photorealistic objects using ray tracing, and is supported by many leading 3D design and content creation applications to accelerate professional workflows.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures touch on content creation and graphics technologies enabled by AI. Qualcomm mentions that generative AI is disrupting 'content creation' methods and enhancing user productivity. NVIDIA describes its RTX platform as enabling '3D design and content creation applications' to 'accelerate and transform their workflows.' While Qualcomm focuses on the disruptive nature of generative AI models (LLMs, LVMs) on content creation broadly, NVIDIA focuses on the specific graphics rendering technology (RTX) that supports professional content creation workflows.

sentences.text: They are disrupting traditional methods of search, content creation, recommendation systems and personalized digital assistants, offering significant enhancements in consumer utility and productivity.

Many leading 3D design and content creation applications developed by our ecosystem partners now support RTX, allowing professionals to accelerate and transform their workflows with NVIDIA RTX GPUs and software.
